top_comments.author: @goodtimes4days
top_comments.text: Cost per outcome still does not measure ROI in one of two categories:  1. Development workflows - this metric shows ROI for development operating costs.  2. Non Dev workflow model operating cost to perform customer workloads impact on the bottom line.  Once development is done, if models are used to run the service there is an entire other world of model selection as you know.  In some cases , fine tuning expensive parts of a workflow will be the only option at times for a decent ROI.  The big story seems to be Dev spend vs operating costs for established applications, but as far as I know, we have these two categories of costs to manage…

You can hardly predict the accuracy of the model when implementing updates or developing a new project.
Usually, midtier to toptier models are the best.
I tried to benchmark the language models on different tasks, but it is still a guessing.
According to my experience, less complex language models need more granular implementation plans.
